articles.title: Jumbo Fed rate-hike warning sends shock waves after inflation surprise
articles.summary: Fed officials signal a more aggressive approach to interest rates amid hotter October CPI inflation.
articles.body:
Today's economic news is short but decidedly not sweet.

Gasoline prices may be easing, but American households are still paying more for groceries, healthcare, and other everyday expenses.

Now, a hotter-than-expected October inflation report has put a potentially much bigger Federal Reserve interest-rate increase on your kitchen table just in time for the holidays.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point (0.5%) rate hike should be considered at the December policymaking meeting.

And Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan also warned that Fed officials may need to move faster and deliver at least two additional increases beginning next month to get inflation under control.

For Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, the stakes are growing. Six months into his leadership, the U.S. central bank's credibility as an inflation fighter is facing a major test.

Following months of waiting for economic data to confirm what American consumers and businesses have known and experienced firsthand — that prices are simply too damn high — the Fed heads into its final meeting of the year Dec. 8-9.

In light of political and economic pressures, it faces a stark choice: increase short-term interest rates to restore its anti-inflation credibility or risk letting price pressures spiral further out of reach.

"(The) Fed is losing its inflation-fighting credibility. Consumers who rely mostly on wages, not their stock portfolios, are paying the price,'' Diane Swonk, chief economist and managing director at KPMG, posted on LinkedIn.

Waller calls for bold action from the Fed on inflation

And those rate hikes could be massive if inflation continues to broaden away from supply shocks and into other sectors, as shown in the hotter-than-expected October Consumer Price Index at 0.4%, up from the 0.3% estimate, CNBC reported.

In October, food, energy, healthcare, recreation, medical care, motor vehicle insurance, and household furnishings all ticked up from the September readout. This is in part due to the geopolitical impact of diesel prices slamming the supply chain, causing businesses to pass along the pain.

Waller, speaking in London on Nov. 10 hours before the CPI release, upped the hawkish tone of the projected tightening cycle and said policymakers needed to take bold action if inflation came in hotter than the consensus forecast, which it did.

"In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting. Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take,'' Waller said in prepared remarks.

articles.title: Voo atrasado ou cancelado: veja quais são os direitos dos passageiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiros podem exigir reembolso, hospedagem, alimentação e transporte; Anac reforça que suporte deve ser imediato.
articles.summary: Passageiro pode exigir reembolso, hospedagem, alimentação e transporte; Anac reforça que suporte deve ser imediato. País paralisou aeroportos e já afeta voos com origem no Brasil.
articles.body:
A Administração Federal de Aviação dos Estados Unidos (FAA, na sigla em inglês) paralisou todos os aeroportos dos Estados Unidos, nesta sexta-feira (13), por motivos de segurança após um problema de comunicação que afeta os centros de controle de tráfego aéreo. Voos com origem no Brasil já sofrem os impactos.

Os passageiros possuem uma série de direitos quando um um voo é cancelado ou atrasado, por qualquer motivo. As companhias aéreas são obrigadas a oferecer assistência aos passageiros.

Dependendo do caso, o cliente pode pedir reembolso ou ter direito a hospedagem, alimentação e acesso à internet, segundo a Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac).

O especialista em Direito Aeronáutico Felipe Bonsenso lembra que a lei exige apoio imediato, mesmo quando o atraso ou cancelamento não é culpa direta da empresa.

"Todos os passageiros devem procurar imediatamente as companhias aéreas e também podem recorrer à Justiça em busca de indenizações, em caso de perdas de eventos ou reuniões, por exemplo", diz.

O que a empresa deve fazer em caso de atraso ou cancelamento?

Segundo a resolução 400 da Anac, a companhia deve avisar o passageiro assim que souber do atraso ou cancelamento. Além disso, ela precisa adotar outras medidas:

manter o passageiro informado , a cada 30 minutos, sobre a previsão de partid a;

oferecer assistência gratuita de acordo com o tempo de espera;

garantir reacomodação, reembolso integral ou transporte alternativo , quando o atraso for maior que 4 horas ou em caso de cancelamento. A opção deve ser escolhida pelo passageiro .

Em caso de atraso, a assistência varia conforme o tempo de espera:

a partir de 1 hora: comunicação (internet, telefone ou outros meios);

a partir de 2 horas: alimentação (voucher ou refeição);

a partir de 4 horas: hospedagem (em caso de pernoite no aeroporto) e transporte . Se o voo for na cidade de residência do passageiro, a empresa pode oferecer apenas o transporte até a casa e de volta ao aeroporto.

Passageiros com Necessidade de Assistência Especial (Pnae) e seus acompanhantes têm direito a hospedagem em qualquer situação.

Um passageiro passa diante de um painel que exibe voos atrasados ​​dentro do terminal, após a Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) dos EUA determinar uma suspensão nacional das decolagens "devido a circunstâncias extraordinárias e por motivos de segurança". A medida ocorreu na sequência de um relato anterior da agência sobre graves problemas nas comunicações de controle de tráfego aéreo no Aeroporto Internacional John F. Kennedy, em Nova York, EUA. — Foto: Angelina Katsanis/Reuters

Se a companhia aérea não oferecer as assistências, isso é considerado um descumprimento do contrato de transporte aéreo , segundo a Anac.

O passageiro deve primeiro procurar os canais de atendimento da empresa. Se não resolver, pode registrar reclamação na plataforma Consumidor.gov.br, usada pelo governo federal.

As queixas registradas nesse canal ajudam a Anac a identificar falhas e reforçar a fiscalização.

Caso o passageiro tenha prejuízos maiores, como a perda de uma entrevista de emprego ou de um casamento, pode pedir indenização além do reembolso. Para isso, deve acionar o Procon.

Se ainda assim ele se sentir insatisfeito, o caminho pode ser a Justiça, que seria o último recurso.

Além da resolução 400 da Anac, o Código de Defesa do Consumidor (CDC) também garante indenização por danos patrimoniais ou morais. Especialistas dizem que ele pode ser utilizado pelos passageiros que se sentirem prejudicados.

“No caso de cancelamento de voo, o artigo 14 do CDC estabelece que o prestador de serviço responde pelos danos que causa ao consumidor”, diz o advogado Rodrigo Alvim, especialista em direito do passageiro e do consumidor.

articles.title: FDA issues recall for honey dietary supplement over undeclared ED ingredient
articles.summary: “The recall was initiated after FDA laboratory testing identified undeclared tadalafil,” the notice said.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — A California-based company has recalled its honey dietary supplement after an undeclared ingredient used to treat erectile dysfunction was discovered in its products.

Eros Apothecary said its Candy Power For Man Organic Honey product contained tadalafil, according to a notice issued by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration .

“The recall was initiated after FDA laboratory testing identified undeclared tadalafil,” the notice said.

“Consumers should stop using Candy Power For Man immediately and dispose of any remaining product,” it continued.

The FDA said the product was sold on eBay between April 27 and July 20, and came in yellow and orange packaging.

Anyone who has experienced health issues after using the product should consult their healthcare provider, the notice stated.

articles.title: DJ Khaled shares he lost 90 pounds with help of GLP-1 drug
articles.summary: In October 2025, Khaled experienced a health scare at a concert, which led to a lifestyle change.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — DJ Khaled shared the reason why he took control of his health.

The producer revealed he lost 90 pounds since last year with the help of the weight loss drug Wegovy.

“The motivation was there, the inspiration was there, working out and trying to eat better, but I needed help,” he told People magazine . “We live for our kids, and our kids make us live. So, I have to do my part.”

Khaled admitted he had to “keep it real” with himself about his weight and spoke to a doctor about taking a GLP-1 .

The “All I Do is Win” performer began his weight loss journey between 295 and 300 pounds and now weighs between 200 and 212 pounds, he told People.

In October 2025, Khaled experienced a health scare at a concert, which led to a lifestyle change.

“There’s a part of my show where I get on my knees and give thanks and show my gratitude,” Khaled said. “So, I get on my knees … but I remember I couldn’t really get up.”

He noted, “One of my friends was coming to me like, ‘Yo, you were breathing hard.’ Then, 10 minutes later, somebody else told me the same thing.

“I said, alright, hold up. … I gotta step my game up. I gotta get my mind right. We can’t have this,” the artist added.

articles.title: Android TV box malware found in 1.3M devices
articles.summary: Google says Videostrong deliberately installed backdoor malware in over 1.3 million Android TV boxes, turning them into a botnet for criminals.
articles.body: You buy a streaming box, plug it into your television and connect it to Wi-Fi. A few minutes later, you're watching your favorite show. Everything seems perfectly normal. But what if that little box has been secretly working for criminals since the day you brought it home? That's the alarming discovery behind a massive Android TV box malware operation involving more than 1.3 million devices worldwide. According to a Nov. 2 report from Google's Threat Intelligence Group, investigators concluded with high confidence that a device manufacturer deliberately installed hidden software inside streaming hardware. That backdoor gave outsiders remote access without the owners knowing. And here's what makes this particularly concerning. The malware was built directly into the devices, and some affected products made it through Google's own security certification process. In other words, buyers could do everything right and still end up with compromised hardware. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. CHEAP ANDROID PHONES FOUND WITH MALWARE ALREADY INSTALLED Google uncovers malware hiding inside Android TV boxes Google says the operation involved Videostrong Technology, a China-based company that manufactures Android-powered devices for different brands. According to investigators, Videostrong developed and installed malicious software called XCPE. Google assesses with high confidence that the company deliberately operated the backdoor for financial gain. The software allowed remote operators to maintain access to devices long after customers purchased them. According to Google, Videostrong sold access to compromised devices to criminal affiliates, who installed additional malware and turned those products into part of a botnet. That's a network of infected devices controlled remotely without their owners' permission. Researchers identified more than 1.3 million affected devices across the globe. Most were Android TV streaming boxes, although the operation also reached other types of connected hardware. And many people using these products had no idea anything was wrong. What criminals were doing with infected streaming boxes While people were watching television, hidden software could be working behind the scenes for someone else. One of the biggest operations involved residential proxy networks. These services allow someone to route their internet activity through another person's home connection. That means a criminal could use your internet address to make suspicious online activity appear to originate from your household. Think about that for a moment. Someone you've never encountered could be using your internet connection without your permission, while your streaming box continues playing Netflix or YouTube. Google also found malware capable of generating fake advertising activity. Some modules secretly loaded ads or simulated interactions to generate revenue for the operators. Other capabilities were more invasive. Researchers observed operators capturing screenshots, injecting keystrokes and collecting sensitive account information from compromised devices. They could also install additional software remotely. And because much of this activity happened in the background, users might never see an obvious warning. 5 WORRISOME PRIVACY CLAUSES HIDDEN IN SMART HOME DEVICES How the Android TV malware bypassed Google's security Normally, manufacturers must pass Google's compatibility and security checks before shipping certified Android devices with Google's services. However, Google says Videostrong found a way around those protections. The company allegedly concealed malicious software during testing. The backdoor then loaded additional malicious code after the device's first startup, exploiting a gap in Google's review process. Even more concerning, the malware could disable Google Play Protect app verification. That's one of Android's built-in defenses against harmful applications. The backdoor also had staying power. Researchers discovered that XCPE was embedded in the device's firmware, the software responsible for basic hardware operations. If someone removed the visible malware package, the system could reinstall it after a reboot. So even a factory reset might leave the underlying infection intact. Which Android TV boxes are affected? This is probably the first question people will ask after hearing about this investigation. Unfortunately, Google has not released a complete consumer-friendly list of every infected retail product. However, cybersecurity company Synthient published its own investigation identifying specific hardware and model names connected to the operation. Confirmed infected streaming box Researchers purchased and examined a MECOOL KM9PRO Max Android TV streaming box in late 2025. They found the XCPE backdoor preinstalled under the package name com.oemservice. The tested device used firmware version C1.0.8_20250325, according to Synthient's technical documentation. This identifies the specific research sample, although it does not establish that every unit running that version is infected. Other device models identified by researchers Synthient also published model identifiers observed in the wider botnet. These include KM9PRO_MAX, KM9PRO, KM2PLUSDELUXE, KM2PLUS, KM7PLUS, KT1, IPx1, IPx3, Q96MAX and TX3MINI. These identifiers appeared in data associated with the malicious operation. However, researchers explicitly warn that a matching model name alone cannot confirm that an individual device is compromised. You can review Synthient's published device model list at github.com/synthient/public-research/blob/main/2026/11/Videostrong/README.md to compare it with your own hardware. The investigation also identified infections in Android-powered karaoke machines, digital signage equipment and some telehealth devices. Google says the malware appeared across many models and brands over several years. And that's why checking the exact product you own is so important. The retail brand on the box may differ from the company responsible for manufacturing its hardware or firmware. Google shuts down the XCPE botnet and bans manufacturer Google worked with Japan's National Police Agency and several cybersecurity companies to dismantle the XCPE operation. Google took legal action to shut down the domains and servers Videostrong used to control infected devices and install malware. The company also pursued legal action against command-and-control domains associated with more than a dozen additional malware families. According to Google, those additional actions were expected to sever criminal access to at least 10 million other compromised devices. That estimate involves malware networks beyond the 1.3 million devices identified in the XCPE operation. Google also cut ties with Videostrong and banned the company, along with future subsidiaries and affiliates, from building or selling certified Android devices or supplying software to other certified vendors. The company says it has also strengthened its security review process to better detect similar threats, including improvements to how it verifies the integrity of firmware on certified Android TV devices. That's encouraging news, but there's an important catch. Disrupting the servers used to control malware doesn't automatically remove malicious firmware from devices already sitting in people's homes. For owners of affected hardware, that leaves an important question about whether their devices can ever be trusted again. How to protect yourself from Android TV box malware Now, before you start unplugging every streaming device in your house, understand that Google has not suggested every Android TV or Google TV product is compromised. However, this investigation offers a good reason to take a closer look at the equipment connected to your home network. 1) Check your streaming box's brand and model Start by identifying the exact make and model of your streaming device. Look on the underside of the box, its original packaging or the device information screen in Settings. Compare that information with Synthient's list of observed models. If your device matches a listed model, investigate further. Remember, a model match alone does not confirm an infection. If you own the MECOOL KM9PRO Max examined by researchers, take the warning seriously and consider replacing it. 2) Disconnect a device you believe is infected If you have strong reason to suspect your streaming box contains malicious firmware, disconnect it from Wi-Fi or unplug it entirely. Contact the manufacturer or retailer about a verified clean firmware update, replacement or refund. Synthient recommends permanently removing affected devices from use because they may contain additional malware. Don't assume a factory reset will solve the problem. The XCPE backdoor was designed to reinstall itself. 3) Check Google Play Protect certification On devices with the Google Play Store, open the Play Store, tap your profile icon and select Settings > About to check the Play Protect certification status. You can also open Play Protect from your profile menu to review security scanning. However, certification alone cannot guarantee a device is free of malware. Some devices associated with this investigation passed Google's certification checks. A certified label offers an additional layer of reassurance, but it cannot guarantee that a device is free of malware. 4) Avoid suspicious streaming apps and cheap TV boxes Be cautious about streaming products promising unlimited premium channels or paid entertainment for a suspiciously low one-time price. The FBI has previously warned about questionable streaming hardware that arrives with malware or installs it during setup. Stick with reputable manufacturers that provide regular security updates. Also, avoid installing streaming applications from unofficial websites or unknown app marketplaces. 5) Keep your home router updated and secure Your router connects your streaming equipment to the rest of your home network. Make sure its firmware is current and review the list of connected devices for unfamiliar equipment. If your router supports a separate guest or smart-home network, consider placing streaming boxes and other connected gadgets there. That can help limit their access to your personal computers and other sensitive devices. If you discover an infected device, disconnect it before changing your Wi-Fi password. A password change alone will not remove malware already embedded in the box. 6) Watch for unusual internet activity Check your router's activity logs or connected-device information if those features are available. Unexplained bandwidth consumption or unfamiliar network connections can be warning signs, although they do not prove a device has malware. Keep in mind that an infected streaming box may show no obvious symptoms. Normal performance doesn't guarantee that the hardware is secure. 7) Protect accounts connected to your streaming device If you've signed into streaming services or a Google account on a device you believe was compromised, change those passwords using a trusted computer or phone. Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) where available. Also, review your account activity for unfamiliar sign-ins. Google observed operators collecting sensitive information from compromised devices, so protecting those accounts is a sensible precaution. 8) Use strong antivirus protection on compatible devices Strong antivirus software can help protect your computers and smartphones from malicious downloads and other threats. Keep those protections enabled, especially when dealing with unfamiliar applications. However, traditional antivirus software on your computer won't remove a backdoor embedded in a streaming box's firmware. If the box itself is compromised, disconnecting and replacing it may be the safest solution. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com 9) Be careful with apps that pay you to share internet bandwidth Some services offer compensation in exchange for allowing others to use your unused internet connection. Google specifically warns that these arrangements can expose devices and home networks to additional security risks. Before installing any bandwidth-sharing or proxy application, understand exactly who can access your connection and what activity they may conduct through it. Kurt's key takeaways What really gets my attention about this investigation is how little someone would have needed to do to become a victim. You could buy a streaming box from an online retailer, connect it to your television and end up with malware that was already installed before you opened the package. And there's another part of this story I find particularly frustrating. Some affected devices made it through Google's certification process. People rely on those certifications because they assume someone has checked the hardware for security problems. In this case, that trust was exploited. Google deserves credit for working with investigators to disrupt the operation. But I think the bigger responsibility starts with manufacturers and the companies selling these products. If a company puts compromised hardware into someone's home, it should be held accountable for fixing the problem. For me, the takeaway is pretty simple. Know what you're connecting to your home network. Stick with brands that have a solid record of security updates. And if researchers confirm that a streaming box contains malicious firmware, I wouldn't keep using it simply because the picture on the television still looks fine. If a streaming box can pass Google's security checks and still arrive with hidden malware, should manufacturers be required to recall compromised devices and compensate customers? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com Sign up for my FREE CyberGuy Newsletter CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Copyright 2026 CyberGuy.com. All rights reserved.

articles.title: Tanker collides with riverboat on Mississippi River at Port of New Orleans
articles.summary: The American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage riverboat was docked at the port when it was struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker Friday afternoon.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS ( WGNO /NEXSTAR) – At least 180 passengers and crew members were rescued Friday after a tanker collided with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River, near the Port of New Orleans.

The American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage riverboat was docked at the port when it was struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker Friday afternoon. The collision caused the boat to partially submerge.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said that 32 people were taken to the hospital, none with critical injuries. Moreno called the rescue “a miracle on the Mississippi.”

“American Cruise Lines can confirm that our riverboat, American Heritage was involved in a collision while it was docked in New Orleans,” a spokesperson for the company said Friday. “We are in close coordination with the U.S. Coast Guard and local authorities. Guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved.”

Video shared to social media, meanwhile, appeared to show the American Heritage riverboat falling to one side, rapidly taking on water. Other images later showed the vessel completely on its side, mostly submerged. Rescue workers could also be seen pulling people to another vessel from the water.

The type of tanker that struck the ship specializes in carrying large quantities of asphalt and bitumen, a semi-solid substance that is often used for road construction and roofing, according to the live shipping tracker MarineTraffic. It is not immediately clear whether the ship was carrying any materials when the crash occurred.

The cruise ship was built in 2015 and originally known as the Queen of the Mississippi before being rebranded as the American Heritage. It is five stories and can hold up to 150 passengers. The paddlewheeler was just finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi when the accident occurred.

Port of New Orleans reported that Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel all responded to the emergency.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

images.caption: Emergency personnel and crews work the scene after a tanker crashed into a river cruise in New Orleans, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. (Enan Chediak/The Advocate via AP)

articles.title: Navy removed naval destroyer commander deployed to Middle East
articles.summary: The U.S. Navy in late September removed a commander of the naval destroyer that was deployed to the Middle East in support of military operations against Iran because of “loss of confidence” after she had been in the job for less than a year, The Hill has learned. Commander of Carrier Strike Group 10, Rear…
articles.body:
The U.S. Navy in late September removed a commander of the naval destroyer that was deployed to the Middle East in support of military operations against Iran because of “loss of confidence” after she had been in the job for less than a year, The Hill has learned.

Commander of Carrier Strike Group 10, Rear Adm. Todd F. Cimicata, relieved Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham of her duties as USS Michael Murphy’s commanding officer on Sept. 27, a Navy official told The Hill on Friday.

Cunningham began her role as the skipper of USS Michael Murphy, an Arleigh Burke-class Aegis guided-missile destroyer, in late October last year before the ship embarked on an 11-month deployment, which ended this week .

The destroyer departed Pearl Harbor on Dec. 1, 2025, operating alongside flagship Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln.

No additional information was available about Cunningham’s removal, which was reported earlier by USNI News .

The USS Michael Murphy helped enforce the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, operating in the north Arabian Sea and Gulf of Oman.

“The Sailors of Michael Murphy demonstrated unmatched grit, professionalism and warfighting excellence during this deployment,” Cmdr. David Nicolas, Michael Murphy’s commanding officer, said in a press release . “Whether defeating incoming air and surface threats or leading operations through contested choke points, this crew never hesitated.”

“They answered every call of our nation, defended our allies, and lived up to the heroic namesake,” Nicolas said. “I could not be prouder of this crew.”

articles.title: Kevin Hassett Says He Will Remain as Trump Economic Adviser
articles.summary: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett denied a report that he plans to depart his post in the coming weeks.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett denied a report that he plans to depart his post in the coming weeks.

"Not true," Hassett said in a text message Friday when asked about the report on his impending departure.

Semafor reported earlier that Hassett is expected leave his role as President Donald Trump's top economic adviser. The news outlet said his potential replacements include Scott Bessent, who would retain his role as Treasury secretary, and Bessent's counselor David Zervos.

Hassett said he joked about the report with the president on Friday afternoon. A White House official also said the report has no factual basis, adding that Hassett is a key member of Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance his policies.

Republican losses in the midterm elections have intensified speculation about a shake-up of the president's team. Days after the midterms, Trump's chief of staff Susie Wiles left and was replaced by Stephen Miller. That move is expected to lead to further changes on the president's staff.

Trump himself has said he expects some turnover among his advisers.

As NEC director, Hassett is responsible for coordinating economic policy across the federal government. A frequent presence on television, Hassett is staunch defender of the president's policies, including his sweeping use of tariff powers, as Trump moved in his second term to reshape US manufacturing and ties with trading partners.

images.caption: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett · Bloomberg · Photographer: Aaron Schwartz/Sipa/Bloomberg

articles.title: US government grounds all flights across the United States 'due to extraordinary circumstances' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop "following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers," which manage the airspace across the United States.
articles.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday afternoon that it has grounded all flights across the United States due to “extraordinary circumstances” and issues related to safety.

The FAA’s website said the cause is an “equipment outage.” The site itself was down for a brief period at the time of publication, with a note that the website was “experiencing technical difficulties.”

Per an alert sent by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center , or ATCSCC, the FAA said the ground stop means that aircraft cannot take off from departure gates. The message said that the disruption was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” but did not specify further. The alert was not visible on the ATCSCC website at press time.

The alert stated that all departing flights must remain on the ground “until further notice.” Inbound international flights will be “managed on a case-by-case basis,” it said.

A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop “following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” which manage the airspace across the United States.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X : “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

It’s not clear what caused the ongoing FAA equipment outage. The outage comes in the same week that the administration rolled out an AI-powered tool for air traffic controllers to save aircraft flight time and fuel costs — though it’s unclear if the ongoing outage is related.

Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that there is “no indication yet that this was a nefarious act,” but warned that the recovery “is going to take some time.”

Updated with comment from the FAA, and remarks from Homeland Security.

images.caption: Image Credits: Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu / Getty Images

articles.title: Fed says it's monitoring the data center build-out for risks to the financial system
articles.summary: The Fed says that in the event of a downturn in artificial intelligence, the defaults on debt could be larger than current balance sheets suggest.
articles.body:
The Federal Reserve is closely monitoring leverage in the rapid data center build-out, noting that in the event of a downturn in artificial intelligence, the defaults on debt could be larger than current balance sheets suggest , according to a report on financial stability released Friday.

Initially, hyperscalers self-funded data centers, with debt issuance having risen to more than $680 billion as of October — a fivefold increase from $130 billion in all of 2023. But now the composition of the debt being issued is evolving from mostly corporate bonds to a combination of public and private debt and structured credit.

In addition, large technology firms are rapidly increasing future lease commitments, backstop guarantees provided to other firms, and other complex and contingent obligations.

A dynamic of circular financing is taking hold that echoes the 2008 financial crisis in which there was mounting debt off firms' balance sheets. The evidence suggests AI firms' economic exposure in the event of a downturn could be larger than their current balance sheets would suggest.

Hyperscaler firms often enter into long-term leases for data center capacity with third-party data center developers. These leases are then used by the third-party developers to secure financing for construction. In addition, graphics processing unit (GPU) makers often provide a guaranteed residual value of the GPU collateral to support purchases of their GPUs by advanced computing technology or large language model (LLM) firms. These debt financings that link hyperscalers and GPU designers with smaller firms are often supplemented by equity investments from the hyperscalers and GPU designers, creating a "circular financing" dynamic.

That's deepening the connection between large hyperscalers and smaller, riskier companies with less access to credit.

The Fed estimates future leases and backstop guarantees for data center build-outs are about $3 trillion now. It says cash outflows for capital expenditures suggest that the pace of the current cycle's investment may surpass that of the 1990s telecom cycle relatively soon.

At the same time, asset valuations across asset classes, from stocks to corporate bonds and real estate, are elevated, and hedge funds have the most leverage since 2013.

Follow Jennifer Schonberger on X @Jenniferisms and on Instagram .

articles.title: Fed’s Jefferson Says Inflation Will Determine Rate Decisions
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation has become the most important measure for policymakers as they consider additional interest-rate h...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation has become the most important measure for policymakers as they consider additional interest-rate hikes.

Recent economic activity and labor market conditions have been solid, while price pressures remained persistent, Jefferson said. Price data for October was consistent with well-above-target inflation, he said.

"Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy," Jefferson said in remarks prepared for a speech in San Diego, adding that policymakers should continue to watch incoming data in considering "further policy adjustments."

Jefferson capped a week of Fed speakers this week who cemented market expectations for an interest-rate increase in December by voicing sharp concerns over price pressures.

A number of other officials called for more rapid policy adjustments than they had previously, including Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who warned that a 50-basis-points move may be needed next month. A few others, however, like Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, stuck with calls for a gradual pace of rate hikes.

Investors are expecting hikes in December and January, and another in either March or April, according to federal funds futures pricing.

In his speech, which was focused on technology and productivity, Jefferson said there's a risk that new technology upends the labor market by putting people out of work before they have an opportunity to retrain. That would force policymakers to asses how much of the increase in joblessness was structural — resulting from a persistent mismatch between workers' skills and employers' needs even with strong economic growth.

"Monetary policy can affect cyclical conditions, like a temporary downturn in employment and spending, but it cannot address the structural factors that determine long-run rates of employment," Jefferson cautioned.

It's also possible the technology boom causes the neutral rate of interest — one that is neither slowing nor stimulating the economy — to rise, Jefferson said. Higher productivity growth that spurs consumer spending and robust investment into the AI buildout may ultimately push the neutral rate higher.

articles.title: Multiple college football teams in flight limbo due to FAA ground stop
articles.summary: The nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration Friday afternoon has impacted travel plans for college football teams scheduled to fly to their destinations. Among teams impacted are four schools in the NCAA’s Big 12 Conference, Baylor University, Kansas State University, University of Utah and Arizona State University; three in the Big Ten…
articles.body:
The nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration Friday afternoon has impacted travel plans for college football teams scheduled to fly to their destinations.

Among teams impacted are four schools in the NCAA’s Big 12 Conference, Baylor University, Kansas State University, University of Utah and Arizona State University; three in the Big Ten — University of Minnesota, Purdue University and University of Washington; as well as the universities of Mississippi, Tennessee and Texas, ESPN reported Friday night.

Teams including Oregon State University, Boise State University, University of North Texas and University of Wyoming were also on flights that were either grounded or never left due to the stop, according to ESPN.

“The safety and well-being of student athletes, coaches, and team personnel remain out highest priority,” the NCAA’s Southeastern Conference wrote in a statement posted to social platform X.

Big 12 Conference, in a separate post to X, wrote it was “evaluating potential changes to Saturday’s football schedule.”

The nationwide grounding began at around 4 p.m. EST and continued into Friday evening. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote in a 4:16 p.m. post on social platform X made the order “following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.”

The FAA lifted the stop at around 8:15 p.m. and airspace reopened, Duffy confirmed during a White House press briefing at around 8:30 p.m., though he clarified the return to normal flight operations is expected to be “slow.”

“It’s going to take us some time to unwind what’s happened this afternoon,” Duffy said.

Duffy attributed the incident to an overload of data on routers, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin adding the “public was never in danger in this process.”

articles.body:
Hegseth directs Pentagon CFO to transform military pay systems

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth directed the Pentagon’s comptroller to begin a “comprehensive transformation” of the military pay systems, arguing the current process has resulted in a growing backlog of “pay challenges.”

“We’ve always wanted to be higher, and a benefits package as a small sign of our appreciation. Our warriors earn every last penny , and we want to make sure that America’s warriors get all the benefits that they deserve,” Hegseth said in a video posted Friday to the social platform X.

Jules “Jay” Hurst III is the Pentagon’s comptroller, who was confirmed by the Senate in early August .

The Defense secretary said the department should not be doing manual tasks at this point and that delayed benefits and payment errors are “unacceptable.”

“That ends today. This is a different department, and our warriors deserve much better,” he said in the 97-second video. “Under the old process, when there was a dispute about the payment, the department actually withheld the usual pay until it was resolved. We’re not doing that anymore.”

Hegseth said the rule now will be that the warfighter is first in principle while the Pentagon figures out what went wrong in the process.

“The best troops in the world deserve the best pay system we can provide, especially in a world where you can do anything with a click on an iPhone,” the Pentagon chief said. “That is exactly what this administration will achieve for our warriors starting now.

articles.body:
The nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration Friday afternoon has been lifted, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said to reporters in the White House briefing room during a press conference that began at around 8:30 p.m. EST.

Duffy added that, although the stoppage is over, the return to normal air traffic will be “slow.”

“The nationwide ground stop has now been lifted, HOWEVER, it will take a long time for traffic to return to normal levels,” air traffic tracker Flightradar wrote in a post on social platform X .

The nationwide grounding began at around 4 p.m.

This story will be updated with additional reporting.

articles.title: Duffy, Mullin call for $50B air travel ‘overhaul’ in fiery ground stop briefing
articles.summary: Trump administration officials reupped their calls for a multi-billion-dollar investment into updating the U.S.’s “incredibly old” air traffic control systems, calling out Congress for “[kicking] the can down the road” on improvements they argued could have prevented Friday night’s nationwide ground stop. “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system,” Transportation Secretary…
articles.body:
Trump administration officials reupped their calls for a multi-billion-dollar investment into updating the U.S.’s “incredibly old” air traffic control systems, calling out Congress for “[kicking] the can down the road” on improvements they argued could have prevented Friday night’s nationwide ground stop.

“What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during the Friday night briefing after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted the stoppage. “Let’s not do a patchwork, a fix to a system that’s critical for every single family.”

“I want $50 billion,” he said, noting President Trump had asked for $30 billion in the past. “Let’s finish this job: new hardware, new software, new telecommunication.”

Duffy in later September asked Congress for $30 billion to fund new technology, control towers and airport improvements across the country. The push came as the FAA began to roll out its Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories — or SMART — program, an AI tool designed to help air traffic controllers anticipate congestion and reduce delays.

The FAA issued the nationwide ground stop at around 4 p.m. EST Friday. The rare protocol was in place for nearly four hours. The agency’s last widespread stoppage, which lasted approximately 90 minutes, was in 2023 due to a contractor outage.

Prior to that, the lasted time the FAA halted all American air travel was on Sept. 11, 2001, in response to the terror attacks — which involved commercial plane hijackings.

During the briefing, Duffy said Friday’s incident was due to an overload of data on routers, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin adding the “public was never in danger in this process.”

“Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data,” Duffy said. “They started to give us inconsistency in the data from those … routers. And because of that, we shut the system down.”

Mullin also said officials have “zero evidence” a cyber-attack led to the telecommunications issue, though he added federal authorities are still investigating the situation.

The stop was lifted at around 8:15 p.m. and airspace reopened, Duffy confirmed during the meeting, though he clarified the return to normal flight operations is expected to be “slow.”

“It’s going to take us some time to unwind what’s happened this afternoon,” Duffy said.

Mullin echoed Duffy’s call for funding to build a new updated system, saying, “It has to be a complete overhaul of the system, which we estimate to be about $50 billion.”

“I think every member of Congress should say yes … every American, I guarantee you, would tell those members, ‘Yes, give President Trump — give Duffy the money. Let them finish this job so we don’t have to do a press conference at 8:30 at night ever again,'” Duffy said.

images.caption: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, left, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, right, speak during a news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room of the White House in Washington, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026

articles.title: AI company behind FAA’s SMART tool denies link to ground stop, Duffy confirms
articles.summary: Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company behind a recently deployed Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) AI tool, denied any link to the nationwide ground stop issued Friday afternoon. “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the company…
articles.body:
Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company behind a recently deployed Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) AI tool, denied any link to the nationwide ground stop issued Friday afternoon.

“The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the company said in a 5:34 p.m. EST post to social platform X , while the stoppage was still in effect.

The nationwide grounding began Friday afternoon and lasted for around four hours. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote in a 4:16 p.m. post on social platform X the FAA made the order “following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.”

The airspace was opened at around 8:15 p.m. and the stop was lifted, Duffy said during a White House briefing that began 15 minutes later. The secretary said the incident resulted from an overload of data on routers.

“Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data,” Duffy said. “They started to give us inconsistency in the data from those … routers. And because of that, we shut the system down.”

The FAA deployed the new Strategic Management of Airspace, Routing and Trajectories — or SMART — tool in September in Washington, D.C. The AI-powered system, which cost the Transportation Department $875 million , is meant to ingest real-time data as well as current and future weather conditions to recommend necessary flight path changes to air traffic controllers, Duffy said at the time.

During Friday’s briefing, the secretary asserted the SMART tool had nothing to do with the ground stop, saying the system “isn’t plugged in.”

“This is completely disconnected , and I love that some people have said this would be the root cause. By the way, if it was, I’ll tell you that, but this is not even plugged in,” he said. “So , there’s no possible way SMART would have impacted.”

Duffy also asked Congress for $50 billion to rebuild what he described as an “incredibly old” air traffic control system, aligning with his ongoing efforts to modernize U.S. air travel. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin echoed Duffy’s call, saying, “It has to be a complete overhaul of the system.”

In September, Duffy had asked the Congress for $30 billion to fund new technology, control towers and airport improvements across the country.
